source.text: Περὶ δὲ τῶν εἰδωλοθύτων, οἴδαμεν ὅτι πάντες γνῶσιν ἔχομεν.

records.literal_gloss: Concerning now the [things] offered to idols, we know that all knowledge we have.

en.L: Now concerning [food] offered to idols: we know that "we all have knowledge."
en.B: Now about food offered to idols. We know, as you say, that "all of us have knowledge."
en.R: Now about food offered to idols. You say, "All of us have knowledge." Yes, we know that.

fr.L: Or, au sujet des [aliments] offerts aux idoles, nous savons que « nous avons tous la connaissance ».
fr.B: Venons-en aux aliments offerts aux idoles. Nous savons, comme vous le dites, que « nous avons tous la connaissance ».
fr.R: Parlons maintenant de la nourriture offerte aux idoles. Vous dites : « Nous avons tous la connaissance. » Oui, nous le savons.

es.L: Ahora bien, acerca de [los alimentos] ofrecidos a los ídolos: sabemos que «todos tenemos conocimiento».
es.B: En cuanto a los alimentos ofrecidos a los ídolos, sabemos, como {{plural_you:ustedes dicen|vosotros decís}}, que «todos tenemos conocimiento».
es.R: Ahora hablemos de los alimentos ofrecidos a los ídolos. {{plural_you:Ustedes dicen|Vosotros decís}}: «Todos tenemos conocimiento». Sí, eso lo sabemos.

decisions.choice: now concerning: Paul takes up the next question the Corinthians raised in their letter
alternatives: a new subject Paul raises on his own
decisions.reason: The same opening, Περὶ δὲ, marks the matters from their letter in 7:1 and 7:25, and again in 12:1 and 16:1. Chapters 8-10 answer this question: may believers eat food that has been offered to idols?

decisions.choice: food offered to idols: meat and other food from animals and offerings sacrificed to pagan gods
alternatives: only meat eaten inside a temple
any food sold in the market
decisions.reason: In a Greek city most meat came from sacrifices. Part of the animal was burned for the god, and the rest was eaten at meals in the temple's dining rooms or sold in the market (10:25). εἰδωλοθύτων is a word used by Jews and Christians and carries disapproval; a pagan host would speak of meat "offered in sacrifice" (10:28). Paul deals with meals in an idol's temple (8:10; 10:14-22) and with sacrificial meat sold or served at home (10:25-30).

decisions.choice: "we all have knowledge" is a saying of the Corinthians, which Paul quotes and agrees with only in part
alternatives: Paul's own statement, with no quotation marks
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT, like all Greek texts, has no quotation marks; ὅτι can introduce the words someone says. Paul quotes the Corinthians' letter elsewhere (7:1; compare 6:12-13). In verse 7 he says that "not everyone has this knowledge", which would contradict himself if verse 1 were his own claim, so the words are best read as their slogan, granted for the moment and then corrected (verses 1b-3).

decisions.choice: knowledge: understanding of the truth about God and the idols, which some in Corinth prized as a mark of spiritual maturity
decisions.reason: γνῶσιν here is the knowledge spelled out in verses 4-6: that an idol is nothing and there is only one God. The Corinthians valued knowledge highly (1:5; 13:2, 8), and some took it as giving them freedom to eat anything.

decisions.choice: [food] offered to idols (L); food offered to idols (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word names what was offered, not only meat, so "food" is the plain English; "offered" covers every kind of offering. The same phrase is used at every level and throughout chapters 8-10. Literal brackets "food", which the Greek leaves understood.

decisions.choice: as you say (B); You say (R)
alternatives: no indication that the words are quoted
decisions.reason: Spoken aloud, quotation marks are not heard, so Balanced and Readable say that these are the Corinthians' words (m3).

decisions.choice: [les aliments] offerts aux idoles (L); les aliments offerts aux idoles (B); la nourriture offerte aux idoles (R) (for chapters 8-10)
alternatives: la nourriture offerte aux idoles at every level
decisions.reason: The word covers everything offered to a god, not only meat (m2), so French says "aliments" rather than "viandes"; "offerts" covers every kind of offering, as the English "offered" does. Readable uses the everyday collective "la nourriture". The same phrase is kept at each level wherever it comes back in chapters 8-10.

decisions.choice: [los alimentos] ofrecidos a los ídolos (L); los alimentos ofrecidos a los ídolos (B, R)
alternatives: la carne ofrecida a los ídolos
decisions.reason: The same words every time the word comes back (8:4, 7, 10; chapter 10), as the English keeps "food offered to idols"; they match Revelation 2:14 and 2:20. "Carne" would narrow the word, which covers any food from the offerings (m2).

decisions.choice: «todos tenemos conocimiento» (L, B); como {{plural_you:ustedes dicen|vosotros decís}} (B); {{plural_you:Ustedes dicen|Vosotros decís}}: «...» (R)
decisions.reason: The Corinthian saying (m3) stands in «» quotation marks, as in 6:12 and 7:1, and Balanced and Readable say whose saying it is, as the English does.

source.text: ἡ γνῶσις φυσιοῖ, ἡ δὲ ἀγάπη οἰκοδομεῖ.

records.literal_gloss: The knowledge puffs up, the but love builds up.

en.L: Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.
en.B: Knowledge puffs a person up, but love builds others up.
en.R: Knowledge makes people proud, but love makes others strong.

fr.L: La connaissance enfle [d’orgueil], mais l’amour édifie.
fr.B: La connaissance enfle d’orgueil celui qui la possède, mais l’amour édifie les autres.
fr.R: La connaissance rend les gens fiers d’eux-mêmes, mais l’amour rend les autres plus forts.

es.L: El conocimiento envanece, pero el amor edifica.
es.B: El conocimiento envanece a la persona, pero el amor edifica a los demás.
es.R: El conocimiento hace que la gente se sienta orgullosa, pero el amor fortalece a los demás.

decisions.choice: puffs up: fills a person with self-importance
decisions.reason: φυσιοῖ is the verb of 4:6, 18-19 and 5:2, pictures something blown up with air. The article on γνῶσις points to knowledge of the kind just claimed: knowledge held as a possession and a source of pride.

decisions.choice: builds up: strengthens others and the church, as a builder raises a house
decisions.reason: οἰκοδομεῖ carries on the building picture of 3:9-17, where the church is God's building. In chapter 14 the same verb describes what helps the gathered church (14:4-5, 12, 17, 26). The contrast is between what swells the self and what strengthens other people.

decisions.choice: Paul's reply to the slogan: a short saying of his own
decisions.reason: The two balanced halves answer "we all have knowledge": knowledge on its own leads to pride, and love is what helps others. Verse 10 turns the word "build up" back on those who have knowledge.

decisions.choice: a person ... others (B); people ... others (R)
alternatives: no objects, as in the Greek
decisions.reason: The Greek verbs have no object. Balanced and Readable supply them to show the contrast in m2: knowledge inflates the one who has it, love strengthens others.

decisions.choice: makes people proud; makes others strong
decisions.reason: Readable says "proud" for this verb throughout 1 Corinthians, and turns the building picture into its plain meaning.

decisions.choice: enfle [d'orgueil] (L), enfle d'orgueil (B), rend fiers d'eux-mêmes (R), as in 5:2; édifie (L, B), rend plus forts (R)
decisions.reason: The verb keeps the wording settled in 5:2. "Édifier" is still current French both for building a house and for strengthening a person (m2), so Literal and Balanced keep the one word that verse 10 turns back ironically on the weak believer. Readable gives the plain sense.

decisions.choice: envanece (L, B), se sienta orgullosa (R); edifica (L, B), fortalece (R)
decisions.reason: "Envanecer" is the word kept for this verb since 4:6, with "sentirse orgulloso" at Readable. "Edificar" is the Spanish word for building up a person or a church, and verse 10 turns on it, so Literal and Balanced keep it; Readable says "fortalece".

source.text: εἴ τις δοκεῖ ἐγνωκέναι τι, οὔπω ἔγνω καθὼς δεῖ γνῶναι·

records.literal_gloss: If anyone thinks to have known something, not yet he knew as it is necessary to know;

en.L: If anyone thinks that {{gender:they have|he has}} come to know something, {{gender:they have|he has}} not yet known as one ought to know.
en.B: If anyone imagines {{gender:they have|he has}} mastered some piece of knowledge, {{gender:they have|he has}} not yet come to know in the way one must.
en.R: Some people think they know a great deal. But they do not yet know in the way they should.

fr.L: Si quelqu’un pense avoir connu quelque chose, il n’a pas encore connu comme il faut connaître.
fr.B: Si quelqu’un s’imagine posséder quelque savoir, il n’a pas encore appris à connaître comme on le doit.
fr.R: Certains pensent qu’ils savent beaucoup de choses. Mais ils ne savent pas encore comme il faudrait savoir.

es.L: Si alguno cree que ha llegado a conocer algo, aún no ha conocido como se debe conocer.
es.B: Si alguien se imagina que domina algún conocimiento, todavía no ha llegado a conocer como es necesario.
es.R: Algunas personas creen que saben mucho. Pero todavía no saben de la manera en que deberían saber.

decisions.choice: thinks that he has come to know: claims to possess knowledge as a finished achievement
decisions.reason: δοκεῖ often means to think or suppose about oneself, sometimes wrongly (3:18; 10:12). The perfect ἐγνωκέναι means to have arrived at knowledge and to hold it. Paul answers with οὔπω ἔγνω: such a person has not yet come to know at all, in the sense that counts.

decisions.choice: as one ought to know: knowing that is joined to love for God and others
decisions.reason: Verse 3 explains what true knowing looks like: it begins with loving God and being known by him. In 13:2 Paul says that knowledge without love is nothing, and in 13:12 that now we know only in part.

decisions.choice: {{gender:they have|he has}}
decisions.reason: τις is anyone at all, man or woman. Readable uses the plural "some people", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: "quelqu'un ... il", with no gender span (for chapters 8-10)
decisions.reason: The English needs {{gender:they have|he has}} for the pronoun after "anyone". In French "quelqu'un" already means any person, man or woman, and the "il" that refers back to it is ordinary generic French, so no setting is needed (style guide 7). The same holds in 8:10.

decisions.choice: ha llegado a conocer, no gender span
decisions.reason: The Spanish verb does not show whether "anyone" is a man or a woman, so the English gender span ({{gender:they have|he has}}) has nothing to change, as in 3:14.

source.text: εἰ δέ τις ἀγαπᾷ τὸν θεόν, οὗτος ἔγνωσται ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: If but anyone loves the God, this [one] has been known by him.

en.L: But if anyone loves God, this [one] has been known by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: But if someone loves God, that person is known by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: But if someone loves God, God knows that person as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own.

fr.L: Mais si quelqu’un aime Dieu, celui-là a été connu par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Mais si quelqu’un aime Dieu, celui-là est connu de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Mais si quelqu’un aime Dieu, Dieu le connaît comme quelqu’un qui {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} appartient.

es.L: Pero si alguno ama a Dios, este ha sido conocido por {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Pero si alguien ama a Dios, esa persona es conocida por {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Pero si alguien ama a Dios, Dios conoce a esa persona como {{deity_pronoun:suya|Suya}}.

decisions.choice: known by God: God has recognized and claimed this person as his own
alternatives: God has information about this person
decisions.reason: In the Old Testament God "knows" those he has chosen (Amos 3:2; Jeremiah 1:5). Paul turns the thought around: what matters is not what a person knows but that God knows them. He makes the same correction in Galatians 4:9, "you have come to know God, or rather to be known by God", and in 13:12. The perfect ἔγνωσται describes a relationship that stands.

decisions.choice: him: God
decisions.reason: αὐτοῦ picks up the nearest person, τὸν θεόν (God), and the passive needs an agent other than the person known.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "if anyone loves God, this one is known by him"
alternatives: "if anyone loves, this one has known" (without "God" and "by him")
decisions.reason: An early papyrus and an early Christian writer are reported to lack "God" and "by him", which would give a saying about love and knowledge rather than about God. Most manuscripts have the longer text, which the SBLGNT follows. Reviewers must check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: God knows that person as his own
alternatives: that person is known by God
decisions.reason: Readable makes the active form plain and says what being known by God means here (m1). Literal and Balanced keep the passive.

decisions.choice: that person
decisions.reason: οὗτος is masculine in form but refers back to "anyone". "That person" is inclusive and needs no setting.

source.text: Περὶ τῆς βρώσεως οὖν τῶν εἰδωλοθύτων οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὐδὲν εἴδωλον ἐν κόσμῳ, καὶ ὅτι οὐδεὶς θεὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς.

records.literal_gloss: Concerning the eating therefore of the [things] offered to idols, we know that nothing [is an] idol in [the] world, and that no God [is] except one.

en.L: So concerning the eating of [food] offered to idols, we know that "an idol [is] nothing in [the] world," and that "[there is] no God except one."
en.B: So, to come back to eating food offered to idols: we know that "no idol in the world is anything real," and that "there is no God except one."
en.R: Now, about eating food offered to idols. You say, "An idol is not real in this world," and "There is only one God." We know that is true.

fr.L: Au sujet donc du fait de manger les [aliments] offerts aux idoles, nous savons qu’« une idole [n’est] rien dans [le] monde » et qu’« [il n’y a] aucun Dieu sinon un seul ».
fr.B: Pour en revenir à la question de manger des aliments offerts aux idoles : nous savons qu’« aucune idole au monde n’a de réalité » et qu’« il n’y a aucun Dieu, sinon un seul ».
fr.R: Revenons à la nourriture offerte aux idoles : peut-on en manger ? Vous dites : « Une idole n’est pas un vrai dieu dans ce monde » et « Il n’y a qu’un seul Dieu. » Nous savons que c’est vrai.

es.L: Así que, acerca del comer de [los alimentos] ofrecidos a los ídolos, sabemos que «un ídolo no [es] nada en [el] mundo» y que «no [hay] Dios sino uno».
es.B: Así que, volviendo a lo de comer alimentos ofrecidos a los ídolos: sabemos que «ningún ídolo en el mundo es algo real» y que «no hay Dios sino uno».
es.R: Ahora bien, sobre comer alimentos ofrecidos a los ídolos. {{plural_you:Ustedes dicen|Vosotros decís}}: «Un ídolo no es nada real en este mundo» y «Solo hay un Dios». Sabemos que eso es verdad.

decisions.choice: so: Paul returns to the question of verse 1 after the aside of verses 1b-3
decisions.reason: οὖν resumes the subject, and the opening Περὶ repeats verse 1, now naming the actual question: the eating of such food.

decisions.choice: both clauses are sayings of the Corinthians, which Paul agrees with
alternatives: Paul's own statements, with no quotation marks
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, οἴδαμεν ὅτι introduces what "we know". These are probably the Corinthians' own words, used to argue that eating is harmless. Paul accepts them as true (verse 6), but in verse 7 he says not everyone knows this, and in 10:19-21 he adds that demons stand behind idol worship.

decisions.choice: an idol is nothing: no idol is a real god; the image stands for a god that does not exist
alternatives: there is no idol in the world
decisions.reason: οὐδὲν εἴδωλον could mean "no idol exists", which is plainly untrue of the images themselves, or "an idol is nothing". The parallel with "no God except one" shows the point: the god the image stands for has no real being. The Old Testament mocks idols the same way (Isaiah 44:9-20; Psalm 115:4-8).

decisions.choice: no God except one: the confession of Israel that God is one
decisions.reason: The words echo Deuteronomy 6:4, "Hear, O Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one", which Jews recited daily, and texts such as Isaiah 44:6 and 45:5. Paul develops this confession in verse 6.

decisions.choice: world: the whole created order
alternatives: the world of people opposed to God
decisions.reason: κόσμῳ here means everything that exists, in heaven and on earth (verse 5): nowhere in it is there any god but one.

decisions.choice: no idol in the world is anything real (B); An idol is not real in this world (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "nothing" means here (m3), so that it is not taken to deny that the images exist. Literal keeps "nothing".

decisions.choice: to come back to (B); You say ... We know that is true (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced signals that the subject of verse 1 resumes (m1). Readable, as in verse 1, says that these are the Corinthians' words (m2).

decisions.choice: «...» y «...» (L, B); {{plural_you:Ustedes dicen|Vosotros decís}}: «...» (R)
decisions.reason: Both sayings of the Corinthians (m2) stand in their own «» marks, as in 8:1, and Readable again says whose sayings they are.

source.text: καὶ γὰρ εἴπερ εἰσὶν λεγόμενοι θεοὶ εἴτε ἐν οὐρανῷ εἴτε ἐπὶ γῆς, ὥσπερ εἰσὶν θεοὶ πολλοὶ καὶ κύριοι πολλοί, ἀλλ’ ἡμῖν εἷς θεὸς ὁ πατήρ, ἐξ οὗ τὰ πάντα καὶ ἡμεῖς εἰς αὐτόν, καὶ εἷς κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, δι’ οὗ τὰ πάντα καὶ ἡμεῖς δι’ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Even for if indeed there are [those] being called gods, whether in heaven or on earth, as there are gods many and lords many, \v 6 yet to us one God the Father, from whom the [things] all and we for him, and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom the [things] all and we through him.

en.L: For even if there are [beings] called gods, whether in heaven or on earth, as indeed there are many gods and many lords, \v 6 yet for us [there is] one God, the Father, from whom [are] all things, and we [are] for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and one Lord, Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, through whom [are] all things, and we [are] through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: There may indeed be beings called gods, whether in heaven or on earth, and in that sense there are many gods and many lords. \v 6 Yet for us there is one God, the Father. Everything has its source in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and our life is directed to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. And there is one Lord, Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. Everything exists through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} we exist.
en.R: People speak of many gods, in heaven and on earth. In fact, they worship many beings they call "gods" and "lords." \v 6 But for us there is only one God, the Father. Everything comes from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and we live for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. And there is only one Lord, Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. God made everything through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and it is through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} that we live.

fr.L: Car même s’il y a [des êtres] appelés dieux, soit dans le ciel, soit sur la terre, comme il y a en effet beaucoup de dieux et beaucoup de seigneurs, \v 6 pour nous pourtant [il y a] un seul Dieu, le Père, de qui [viennent] toutes choses, et nous [sommes] pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et un seul Seigneur, Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, par qui [sont] toutes choses, et nous [sommes] par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Il se peut qu’il y ait des êtres qu’on appelle dieux, dans le ciel ou sur la terre, et en ce sens il existe beaucoup de dieux et beaucoup de seigneurs. \v 6 Mais pour nous, il n’y a qu’un seul Dieu, le Père. Tout a en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} sa source, et notre vie est tournée vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Et il n’y a qu’un seul Seigneur, Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}. Tout existe par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et c’est par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} que nous existons.
fr.R: Les gens parlent de beaucoup de dieux, dans le ciel et sur la terre. En fait, ils adorent beaucoup d’êtres qu’ils appellent « dieux » et « seigneurs ». \v 6 Mais pour nous, il n’y a qu’un seul Dieu, le Père. Tout vient de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et nous vivons pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Et il n’y a qu’un seul Seigneur, Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}. Dieu a tout créé par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et c’est grâce à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} que nous vivons.

es.L: Porque aunque haya [seres] llamados dioses, ya sea en el cielo o en la tierra, como de hecho hay muchos dioses y muchos señores, \v 6 para nosotros, sin embargo, [hay] un solo Dios, el Padre, de quien [proceden] todas las cosas, y nosotros [somos] para {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}; y un solo Señor, {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, por medio de quien [son] todas las cosas, y nosotros [somos] por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Puede que haya seres llamados dioses, ya sea en el cielo o en la tierra, y en ese sentido hay muchos dioses y muchos señores. \v 6 Pero para nosotros hay un solo Dios, el Padre. Todo tiene su origen en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y nuestra vida está dirigida hacia {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Y hay un solo Señor, {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. Todo existe por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} existimos nosotros.
es.R: La gente habla de muchos dioses, en el cielo y en la tierra. De hecho, adoran a muchos seres a los que llaman «dioses» y «señores». \v 6 Pero para nosotros hay un solo Dios, el Padre. Todo viene de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y vivimos para {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Y hay un solo Señor, {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. Dios hizo todo por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y es por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} que vivimos.

decisions.choice: even if there are so-called gods: Paul grants that many are called gods and treated as such, without granting that they are gods
alternatives: Paul admits that other gods really exist
Paul denies that anything stands behind idols
decisions.reason: εἴπερ ("if indeed") and λεγόμενοι ("called") keep a distance: these are gods in name. ὥσπερ then grants that in practice there are many: people worship them, and they hold power over their worshipers. Paul will say in 10:20 that what pagans sacrifice they offer to demons, not to God.

decisions.choice: gods and lords: the gods of Greek and Roman religion, and other powers given divine honor
decisions.reason: Corinth had temples to many gods, among them Apollo, Aphrodite, Poseidon and Asclepius, and the worship of the emperor was growing. κύριοι ("lords") was a title given to gods of the cults and to rulers. "In heaven or on earth" covers gods of the sky and gods of land and underworld, and perhaps rulers honored as divine.

decisions.choice: one God ... one Lord: the confession that God is one (Deuteronomy 6:4), with "God" said of the Father and "Lord" said of Jesus Christ
alternatives: two separate confessions with no link to Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: The Greek Old Testament renders Deuteronomy 6:4 with the words θεός, κύριος and εἷς: "the Lord our God, the Lord is one". There "Lord" stands for the divine name. Paul keeps "one" twice and divides the confession: the one God is the Father, the one Lord is Jesus Christ. He has just quoted the same confession in verse 4.

decisions.choice: Jesus Christ shares the identity of the one God: he is named within Israel's confession and given a part in creation
alternatives: Christ as a second, lesser divine being beside God
decisions.reason: Paul is not adding a second god; he is denying that there are many (verse 4). He places Jesus within the confession of the one God, gives him the title that stood for the divine name, and says all things exist through him, as John 1:3, Colossians 1:16 and Hebrews 1:2 also do. The Father remains the source of all things. Compare Philippians 2:9-11, where the name above every name is given to Jesus.

decisions.choice: from the Father, for the Father, through Christ: the source, the goal and the agent of all things
alternatives: all four phrases about creation only
decisions.reason: The clauses have no verbs. ἐξ οὗ ("from whom") makes the Father the source of everything, and εἰς αὐτόν ("for him") the goal of our life. δι οὗ ("through whom") makes Christ the one through whom everything came to be. The last phrase, ἡμεῖς δι αὐτοῦ, most likely includes our new life as God's people, since Paul speaks of new creation through Christ (2 Corinthians 5:17-18); "we" here are believers.

decisions.choice: for us: in the confession and life of believers, in contrast to those who worship many gods
alternatives: "in our opinion", as if one God were true only for believers
decisions.reason: ἡμῖν sets believers against the worshipers of many gods in verse 5. Verse 4 has already said that there is no God except one, so Paul is not making truth a matter of opinion.

decisions.choice: [there is] ... [are] (L); there is, has its source in, is directed to, exists (B); comes from, live for, made, live (R)
alternatives: verbless phrases, as in the Greek
decisions.reason: English needs verbs where the Greek has none. Literal brackets them; Balanced and Readable choose verbs that keep the sense of each preposition (m5). Readable names God as the maker in "God made everything through him", as Colossians 1:16 does.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L), {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Pronoun and title settings, for the Father and for Jesus Christ alike.

decisions.choice: they worship many beings they call "gods" and "lords"
alternatives: there are many gods and many lords
decisions.reason: Readable says in what sense there are many gods (m1), so that it does not sound as if Paul believes in them.

decisions.choice: un solo Dios ... un solo Señor
decisions.reason: Spanish "un Dios" could be heard as "a god", one among others; "un solo" makes the number the point, as the confession that God is one does (m3).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}
decisions.reason: As recorded at 1:1, "Jesus Christ" is one span, "Jesucristo" or "Jesús, el Mesías", at every level.

source.text: Ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐν πᾶσιν ἡ γνῶσις· τινὲς δὲ τῇ συνηθείᾳ ἕως ἄρτι τοῦ εἰδώλου ὡς εἰδωλόθυτον ἐσθίουσιν, καὶ ἡ συνείδησις αὐτῶν ἀσθενὴς οὖσα μολύνεται.

records.literal_gloss: But not in all [is] the knowledge; some but by the habit until now of the idol as [a thing] offered to an idol eat, and the conscience of them weak being is defiled.

en.L: But the knowledge [is] not in all; and some, by [their] habit with the idol until now, eat [food] as offered to an idol, and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.
en.B: But not all have this knowledge. Some, from long habit with the idol up to the present, still eat the food as something offered to an idol; and their conscience, which is weak, is soiled.
en.R: But not every believer knows this. Some used to worship idols, and they are still used to them. So when they eat this food, they think of it as food given to an idol. Their conscience is weak, so eating it makes their conscience unclean.

fr.L: Mais la connaissance [n’est] pas en tous ; et certains, par l’habitude de l’idole jusqu’à maintenant, mangent [l’aliment] comme offert à une idole, et leur conscience, étant faible, est souillée.
fr.B: Mais tous n’ont pas cette connaissance. Certains, habitués à l’idole depuis longtemps et jusqu’à présent, mangent encore cet aliment comme une chose offerte à une idole ; et leur conscience, qui est faible, en est salie.
fr.R: Mais tous les croyants ne savent pas cela. Certains adoraient des idoles autrefois, et ils en ont encore l’habitude. Alors, quand ils mangent cette nourriture, ils pensent qu’elle a été donnée à une idole. Leur conscience est faible, et manger cette nourriture la rend impure.

es.L: Pero no en todos [está] el conocimiento; y algunos, por la costumbre con el ídolo hasta ahora, comen [el alimento] como ofrecido a un ídolo, y su conciencia, siendo débil, se contamina.
es.B: Pero no todos tienen este conocimiento. Algunos, por su larga costumbre con el ídolo hasta el presente, todavía comen el alimento como algo ofrecido a un ídolo; y su conciencia, que es débil, queda manchada.
es.R: Pero no todos los creyentes saben esto. Algunos antes adoraban ídolos, y todavía están acostumbrados a ellos. Por eso, cuando comen este alimento, piensan en él como alimento ofrecido a un ídolo. Su conciencia es débil, y por eso comerlo hace que su conciencia quede manchada.

decisions.choice: this knowledge: the knowledge of verses 4-6, that idols are nothing and God is one
decisions.reason: The article on γνῶσις points back to the knowledge just set out. "Not in all" corrects the slogan of verse 1, "we all have knowledge".

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "by habit"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read a word for "conscience" in place of συνηθείᾳ ("habit"); the two look alike in Greek, and "conscience" comes later in the verse. Several of the oldest manuscripts read "habit", which the SBLGNT follows. Reviewers must check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: some: believers who had worshiped idols until they came to faith, and still feel that the idol is real
decisions.reason: Most of the church in Corinth had been pagans (12:2). For people who had eaten sacrificial meals all their lives, eating such food could still feel like taking part in the idol's worship.

decisions.choice: conscience: inner awareness that judges one's own conduct
decisions.reason: συνείδησις is the inner sense that approves or condemns what a person does (2 Corinthians 1:12; 4:2). Here it tells these believers that eating is idolatry.

decisions.choice: weak: not fully convinced, and so easily troubled and led astray
decisions.reason: ἀσθενὴς describes a conscience that cannot yet act on the truth that idols are nothing. The word may have been the Corinthians' label for these believers; Paul uses it, but he takes their side (verses 9-13).

decisions.choice: is defiled: is stained with guilt, because they do what they believe is wrong
alternatives: is made ritually impure by the food itself
decisions.reason: μολύνεται means to soil or stain. The food itself does not defile (verse 8); the harm comes from acting against conscience, which for them is sin (compare Romans 14:14, 23).

decisions.choice: soiled (B); makes their conscience unclean (R)
decisions.reason: "Defiled" is now rare outside church use. Balanced and Readable use plain words for staining; Literal keeps "defiled".

decisions.choice: every believer; Some used to worship idols, and they are still used to them
alternatives: Some, by habit with the idol until now
decisions.reason: Readable says who "some" are and what their habit was (m3).

decisions.choice: conciencia, débil (8:7-12)
decisions.reason: "Conciencia" and "débil" are kept at every level through the chapter, as the English keeps "conscience" and "weak", so the argument can be followed word by word.

decisions.choice: se contamina (L); queda manchada (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb is a stain of guilt (m6). Literal says "contaminarse", the word for ritual defilement; Balanced and Readable say "manchada", a stain, as the English says "soiled" and "unclean".

source.text: βρῶμα δὲ ἡμᾶς οὐ παραστήσει τῷ θεῷ· οὔτε γὰρ ἐὰν φάγωμεν, περισσεύομεν, οὔτε ἐὰν μὴ φάγωμεν, ὑστερούμεθα.

records.literal_gloss: Food but us not will present to the God; neither for if we eat, do we abound, nor if not we eat, do we lack.

en.L: But food will not present us to God; for neither, if we eat, do we abound, nor, if we do not eat, do we lack.
en.B: Food will not decide how we stand before God: we gain nothing by eating, and we lose nothing by not eating.
en.R: What we eat does not bring us closer to God. God does not think more of us if we eat, or less of us if we do not eat.

fr.L: Or un aliment ne nous présentera pas à Dieu ; car si nous mangeons, nous n’avons rien de plus, et si nous ne mangeons pas, nous n’avons rien de moins.
fr.B: Ce n’est pas la nourriture qui décidera de notre position devant Dieu : nous ne gagnons rien à manger, et nous ne perdons rien à ne pas manger.
fr.R: Ce que nous mangeons ne nous rapproche pas de Dieu. Dieu ne nous estime pas davantage si nous mangeons, ni moins si nous ne mangeons pas.

es.L: Pero el alimento no nos presentará ante Dios; porque ni si comemos tenemos de más, ni si no comemos tenemos de menos.
es.B: La comida no decide cómo estamos ante Dios: no ganamos nada por comer, ni perdemos nada por no comer.
es.R: Lo que comemos no nos acerca a Dios. Dios no piensa mejor de nosotros si comemos, ni peor si no comemos.

decisions.choice: present us to God: give us a standing before God, as when someone is brought before him
alternatives: bring us near to God in worship
decisions.reason: παραστήσει means to bring someone forward or present them, and Paul uses it of being presented before God at the end (2 Corinthians 4:14; Romans 14:10). Food gives no one any standing with God, either for or against.

decisions.choice: not marked as a quotation: Paul's own statement, though it may echo the Corinthians
alternatives: "Food will not present us to God" as another Corinthian slogan
decisions.reason: Some read the first clause as the Corinthians' words, since it states the case of those who eat freely. Paul agrees with it, but he draws a different conclusion: since eating gains nothing, giving it up for others loses nothing (verses 9-13). The meaning of the sentence is the same either way.

decisions.choice: abound ... lack: have an advantage ... be at a disadvantage, before God
decisions.reason: περισσεύομεν means to have more than enough and ὑστερούμεθα to fall short. Here they refer to standing before God, the subject of the first clause.

decisions.choice: decide how we stand before God; gain ... lose (B); bring us closer to God; think more of us ... less of us (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the verbs mean here (m1, m3); Literal keeps their form.

source.text: βλέπετε δὲ μή πως ἡ ἐξουσία ὑμῶν αὕτη πρόσκομμα γένηται τοῖς ἀσθενέσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Watch but lest somehow the right of you this a stumbling block become to the weak.

en.L: But watch out, lest this right of yours somehow become a stumbling block to the weak.
en.B: But be careful that this right you have does not trip up those who are weak.
en.R: But be careful. Do not let your right to eat this food trip up people whose conscience is weak.

fr.L: Mais prenez garde que ce droit qui est le vôtre ne devienne d’une manière ou d’une autre une pierre d’achoppement pour les faibles.
fr.B: Mais faites attention que ce droit que vous avez ne fasse pas trébucher ceux qui sont faibles.
fr.R: Mais faites attention. Votre droit de manger cette nourriture ne doit pas faire trébucher ceux dont la conscience est faible.

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:miren|mirad}} que {{plural_you:este derecho de ustedes|este derecho vuestro}} no llegue a ser de algún modo tropiezo para los débiles.
es.B: Pero {{plural_you:tengan|tened}} cuidado de que este derecho que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} no haga tropezar a los que son débiles.
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:tengan|tened}} cuidado. No {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} que {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} derecho a comer este alimento haga tropezar a quienes tienen la conciencia débil.

decisions.choice: this right of yours: the freedom to eat, which those with knowledge claimed
decisions.reason: ἐξουσία is the right or freedom to do something. αὕτη ("this") may keep a distance: the right you claim. In chapter 9 Paul shows how he gives up his own rights (9:4-6, 12, 18) for the sake of others.

decisions.choice: a stumbling block: something that makes a person trip, that is, leads them into sin
decisions.reason: πρόσκομμα is an obstacle one strikes a foot against. Verses 10-11 show what is meant: the weak believer is led to act against conscience and is harmed (compare Romans 14:13, 20).

decisions.choice: trip up (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the noun into a plain verb; Literal keeps "stumbling block".

decisions.choice: your right to eat this food; people whose conscience is weak
alternatives: this right of yours; the weak
decisions.reason: Readable says what the right is (m1) and who the weak are (verse 7).

decisions.choice: le droit at every level (for chapters 8-9); une pierre d'achoppement (L), faire trébucher (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Droit" names what the Corinthians claimed (m1) and is the word Paul's own rights as an apostle take up in chapter 9. "Pierre d'achoppement" is the established French picture of a stone a walker trips on; Balanced and Readable say it with the plain verb, as the English does.

decisions.choice: derecho
decisions.reason: The word is a right one is entitled to (m1). Spanish says "derecho" at every level, as the English says "right", ready for the apostle's rights in chapter 9; "libertad" is kept for being free.

decisions.choice: tropiezo (L); hacer tropezar (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Romans 14:13 and 14:20: Literal keeps the noun "tropiezo", and Balanced and Readable say "hacer tropezar", trip up.

source.text: ἐὰν γάρ τις ἴδῃ σὲ τὸν ἔχοντα γνῶσιν ἐν εἰδωλείῳ κατακείμενον, οὐχὶ ἡ συνείδησις αὐτοῦ ἀσθενοῦς ὄντος οἰκοδομηθήσεται εἰς τὸ τὰ εἰδωλόθυτα ἐσθίειν;

records.literal_gloss: If for anyone sees you the [one] having knowledge in an idol's temple reclining, not the conscience of him weak being will be built up to the [things] offered to idols to eat?

en.L: For if anyone sees you, the one who has knowledge, reclining [at table] in an idol's temple, will not {{gender:their|his}} conscience, since {{gender:they are|he is}} weak, be built up to eat [food] offered to idols?
en.B: For suppose someone who is weak sees you, the one with knowledge, reclining at a meal in an idol's temple. Will that not "build up" {{gender:their|his}} conscience, so that {{gender:they go|he goes}} on to eat food offered to idols?
en.R: Suppose a believer with a weak conscience sees you eating in an idol's temple, because you know that idols are not real. Then {{gender:they|he}} will be encouraged to eat food offered to idols too, even though {{gender:they think|he thinks}} it is wrong.

fr.L: Car si quelqu’un te voit, toi qui as la connaissance, attablé dans un temple d’idole, sa conscience, puisqu’il est faible, ne sera-t-elle pas édifiée jusqu’à manger les [aliments] offerts aux idoles ?
fr.B: Suppose en effet que quelqu’un de faible te voie, toi qui as la connaissance, prendre part à un repas dans le temple d’une idole. Sa conscience ne va-t-elle pas être « édifiée », au point qu’il ira manger des aliments offerts aux idoles ?
fr.R: Imagine qu’un croyant à la conscience faible te voie manger dans le temple d’une idole, parce que tu sais que les idoles ne sont pas de vrais dieux. Alors il se sentira encouragé à manger lui aussi de la nourriture offerte aux idoles, même s’il pense que c’est mal.

es.L: Porque si alguno te ve a ti, el que tiene conocimiento, reclinado [a la mesa] en el templo de un ídolo, ¿no será edificada su conciencia, siendo débil, para comer [alimentos] ofrecidos a los ídolos?
es.B: Supongamos que alguien débil te ve a ti, que tienes conocimiento, reclinado a la mesa en el templo de un ídolo. ¿No «edificará» eso su conciencia, de modo que llegue a comer alimentos ofrecidos a los ídolos?
es.R: Supongamos que un creyente con la conciencia débil te ve comiendo en el templo de un ídolo, porque tú sabes que los ídolos no son reales. Entonces se animará a comer también alimentos ofrecidos a los ídolos, aunque piense que está mal.

decisions.choice: reclining in an idol's temple: eating a meal in the dining rooms of a pagan temple
decisions.reason: Temples had dining rooms where people held meals for festivals, family celebrations and the meetings of trade groups and clubs; such meals were part of ordinary social life. κατακείμενον means to recline, the usual posture at a formal meal. εἰδωλείῳ is a Jewish and Christian word for a temple of an idol.

decisions.choice: will be built up: encouraged, but in the wrong direction, to their harm
decisions.reason: οἰκοδομηθήσεται is the verb of verse 1, "love builds up". Paul uses it with irony: the example of the one with knowledge does "build up" the weak, but only to do what their conscience condemns. Some in Corinth may have argued that eating would strengthen the weak; if so, Paul turns their word against them.

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer yes
decisions.reason: οὐχὶ introduces a question expecting agreement: of course it will.

decisions.choice: you, who have knowledge: Paul turns to one member of the group that claims knowledge
decisions.reason: σὲ is singular, and τὸν ἔχοντα γνῶσιν names the person by the claim of verse 1. The weak one sees what the knowing one does, not what that person knows.

decisions.choice: "build up", in quotation marks
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the word of verse 1 and marks the irony (m2). Literal keeps "built up"; Readable says "encouraged" and adds what makes it harmful.

decisions.choice: a believer; because you know that idols are not real; even though they think it is wrong
decisions.reason: Readable says who is watching (verse 11 calls this person a brother), what the knowledge is (verse 4), and why the example does harm (verse 7).

decisions.choice: {{gender:their|his}} and related forms
decisions.reason: τις is anyone, man or woman, so the pronouns that refer to this person take the gender setting.

decisions.choice: "te", "toi", "tu" (and "ta connaissance" in 8:11)
decisions.reason: The Greek pronoun is singular: Paul turns to one member of the group that claims knowledge (m4). English "you" does not show this; French follows the Greek number with "tu" (style guide 6), and returns to "vous" in 8:12, where the Greek is plural.

decisions.choice: te ... tú, no plural_you setting; su conciencia, no gender span
decisions.reason: Paul turns to one member of the group that claims knowledge (m4), so Spanish uses "tú", which takes no ustedes/vosotros setting. Spanish "su" and the verbs that follow do not show whether the weak believer is a man or a woman, so the English gender spans have nothing to change.

decisions.choice: «edificará»
decisions.reason: Balanced puts "edificar" in quotation marks, as the English does with "build up": it is the word of verse 1 used in irony (m2).

source.text: ἀπόλλυται γὰρ ὁ ἀσθενῶν ἐν τῇ σῇ γνώσει, ὁ ἀδελφὸς δι’ ὃν Χριστὸς ἀπέθανεν.

records.literal_gloss: Is destroyed for the [one] being weak by the your knowledge, the brother for whom Christ died.

en.L: For the one who is weak is destroyed by your knowledge, the {{gender:brother or sister|brother}} for whom {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} died.
en.B: And so, through your knowledge, the one who is weak is ruined: a {{gender:brother or sister|brother}} for whom {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} died.
en.R: Then your knowledge will bring ruin on that weak {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}, someone {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} died for.

fr.L: Car celui qui est faible périt par ta connaissance, {{gender:le frère ou la sœur|le frère}} pour qui le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} est mort.
fr.B: Et ainsi, par ta connaissance, celui qui est faible va à sa perte : {{gender:un frère ou une sœur|un frère}} pour qui le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} est mort.
fr.R: Alors ta connaissance va causer la perte de {{gender:ce frère ou de cette sœur|ce frère}} à la conscience faible, quelqu’un pour qui le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} est mort.

es.L: Porque el que es débil es destruido por tu conocimiento, el hermano por quien {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} murió.
es.B: Y así, por tu conocimiento, se arruina el que es débil: un hermano por quien {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} murió.
es.R: Entonces tu conocimiento llevará a la ruina a ese hermano débil, alguien por quien {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} murió.

decisions.choice: is destroyed: is ruined in faith, led away from Christ
alternatives: loses eternal life without hope of return
decisions.reason: ἀπόλλυται is the word Paul uses for those who are perishing (1:18). Here it describes the serious spiritual harm done when a believer is led back into what they see as idolatry; the present tense describes a process under way. How final this ruin is Paul does not say; Romans 14:15 gives the same warning.

decisions.choice: by your knowledge: the very knowledge you are proud of is the means of the harm
decisions.reason: ἐν with the dative marks the means. σῇ ("your") is singular, as in verse 10, and sharpens the irony: the knowledge that should help has become a weapon.

decisions.choice: brother: a fellow believer, man or woman
decisions.reason: ἀδελφὸς is masculine, but in Paul's letters it names any member of God's family, as the plural does throughout the letter.

decisions.choice: for whom Christ died: the weak believer's worth is measured by Christ's death for him
decisions.reason: δι ὃν ("for whom") gives the reason this harm matters: Christ gave his life for this person, and the one with knowledge will not give up a meal. Romans 14:15 makes the same appeal.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}
decisions.reason: Paul means any fellow believer (m3). The singular form keeps the family word Paul uses, as the plural "brothers and sisters" does; "brother" remains as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: is ruined (B); bring ruin on (R)
decisions.reason: "Destroyed" in English sounds like physical destruction. "Ruined" keeps the seriousness without deciding how final the loss is (m1). Literal keeps "destroyed".

decisions.choice: {{gender:le frère ou la sœur|le frère}}, with the determiner inside the span (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: French gives each noun its own article or possessive ("le frère ou la sœur", "mon frère ou ma sœur"), so the span holds the determiner too, as in Romans 14. The plural keeps the usual {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}.

decisions.choice: hermano, no setting
decisions.reason: As in 5:11 and Romans 14:15, Spanish "hermano" for a fellow believer covers a man or a woman (m3), so the English gender span has no Spanish counterpart; the same in verses 12-13.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}
decisions.reason: Spanish cannot say "Mesías murió" without the article, so even Literal writes "el Mesías" in the alternative, as Romans 14:15 does.

source.text: οὕτως δὲ ἁμαρτάνοντες εἰς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ τύπτοντες αὐτῶν τὴν συνείδησιν ἀσθενοῦσαν εἰς Χριστὸν ἁμαρτάνετε.

records.literal_gloss: Thus but sinning against the brothers and striking their conscience being weak against Christ you sin.

en.L: And by sinning in this way against the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} and striking their conscience, which is weak, you sin against {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: When you sin like this against your {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} and deal a blow to their weak conscience, you are sinning against {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: When you sin against your {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} like this and hurt their weak conscience, you are sinning against {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.

fr.L: Et en péchant ainsi contre les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} et en frappant leur conscience, qui est faible, vous péchez contre le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Quand vous péchez ainsi contre vos {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} et que vous portez un coup à leur conscience déjà faible, c’est contre le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} que vous péchez.
fr.R: Quand vous péchez ainsi contre vos {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} et que vous faites du mal à leur conscience faible, vous péchez contre le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}.

es.L: Y pecando así contra los hermanos y golpeando su conciencia, que es débil, contra {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} {{plural_you:pecan|pecáis}}.
es.B: Cuando {{plural_you:pecan|pecáis}} así contra {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} hermanos y {{plural_you:golpean|golpeáis}} su conciencia débil, {{plural_you:están|estáis}} pecando contra {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}.
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:pecan|pecáis}} así contra {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} hermanos y {{plural_you:hieren|herís}} su conciencia débil, {{plural_you:están|estáis}} pecando contra {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} mismo.

decisions.choice: striking: dealing a blow to a conscience already weak
decisions.reason: τύπτοντες means to strike or beat. The picture is of hitting someone who is already frail: the harm is real and wounds the person, not merely their feelings.

decisions.choice: sinning against Christ: Christ is so joined to his people that harm done to them is done to him
decisions.reason: Paul himself heard the risen Lord say, "why are you persecuting me?" (Acts 9:4-5), and Jesus taught that what is done to the least of his family is done to him (Matthew 25:40). In 12:12-27 Paul describes the church as Christ's body.

decisions.choice: brothers: fellow believers, women and men
decisions.reason: The plural, as throughout the letter, means the members of God's family.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: As throughout the letter. Balanced and Readable add "your", which the article implies.

decisions.choice: deal a blow to (B); hurt (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of a blow; Readable uses a plain word. Literal keeps "striking".

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}
decisions.reason: Readable adds "himself" to bring out the point of m2: the sin reaches Christ in person.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} mismo, no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Where the English Readable says "Christ himself", Spanish says "Cristo mismo", where "mismo" is an adjective, not a pronoun, and takes no span.

source.text: διόπερ εἰ βρῶμα σκανδαλίζει τὸν ἀδελφόν μου, οὐ μὴ φάγω κρέα εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, ἵνα μὴ τὸν ἀδελφόν μου σκανδαλίσω.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore if food causes to fall the brother of me, by no means will I eat meat to the age, so that not the brother of me I cause to fall.

en.L: Therefore, if food causes my {{gender:brother or sister|brother}} to fall, I will by no means eat meat for ever, so that I do not cause my {{gender:brother or sister|brother}} to fall.
en.B: That is why, if food causes my {{gender:brother or sister|brother}} to fall, I will not eat meat as long as I live, so that I will not be what makes my {{gender:brother or sister|brother}} fall.
en.R: So if food leads my {{gender:brother or sister|brother}} into sin, I will not eat meat ever again. I refuse to be the one who makes my {{gender:brother or sister|brother}} fall.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi, si un aliment fait tomber {{gender:mon frère ou ma sœur|mon frère}}, je ne mangerai plus du tout de viande, à jamais, afin de ne pas faire tomber {{gender:mon frère ou ma sœur|mon frère}}.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi, si un aliment fait tomber {{gender:mon frère ou ma sœur|mon frère}}, je ne mangerai plus de viande de toute ma vie, pour ne pas être celui qui fait tomber {{gender:mon frère ou ma sœur|mon frère}}.
fr.R: Alors, si de la nourriture entraîne {{gender:mon frère ou ma sœur|mon frère}} dans le péché, je ne mangerai plus jamais de viande. Je refuse d’être celui qui fait tomber {{gender:mon frère ou ma sœur|mon frère}}.

es.L: Por lo cual, si un alimento hace caer a mi hermano, no comeré carne nunca jamás, para no hacer caer a mi hermano.
es.B: Por eso, si la comida hace caer a mi hermano, no comeré carne mientras viva, para no ser yo quien haga caer a mi hermano.
es.R: Así que, si la comida lleva a mi hermano a pecar, no volveré a comer carne nunca más. No quiero ser yo el que haga caer a mi hermano.

decisions.choice: cause to fall: lead a believer into sin, here by acting against conscience
decisions.reason: σκανδαλίζει comes from a word for a trap or snare. It means to cause someone to sin or to fall away (Matthew 18:6; Romans 14:21). Here it sums up verses 10-12: the weak believer is drawn into what they believe is idolatry.

decisions.choice: by no means ... for ever: never again, as long as I live
decisions.reason: οὐ μὴ is the strongest Greek denial, and εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα means "for ever". Together they make a vow-like statement.

decisions.choice: meat: any meat, not only meat offered to idols
decisions.reason: Paul moves from the general βρῶμα ("food") to κρέα ("meat"), going beyond the case in question: rather than harm a fellow believer, he would give up meat altogether.

decisions.choice: Paul speaks in the first person: he offers himself as the example
decisions.reason: After addressing "you" in verses 9-12, Paul says what he himself will do. Chapter 9 develops this example: Paul gives up his rights for the sake of the gospel and of others.

decisions.choice: my brother: any fellow believer, man or woman
decisions.reason: As in verse 11, the singular means a member of God's family.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brother or sister|brother}}
decisions.reason: As in verse 11.

decisions.choice: cause to fall (L, B); leads into sin, makes fall (R)
decisions.reason: "Offend" in current English means to upset someone, which is not the point (m1). "Fall" keeps the picture of the trap; Readable also says what the fall is.

decisions.choice: as long as I live (B); ever again (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means for a person (m2).

decisions.choice: faire tomber (L, B, R); entraîner dans le péché (R) (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: "Scandaliser" in current French means to shock or offend someone, which is not the point (m1). "Faire tomber" keeps the picture of the fall into sin, and Readable also says what the fall is, as the English does.

decisions.choice: hacer caer (L, B); llevar a pecar, hacer caer (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means leading a believer into sin (m1). "Escandalizar" in today's Spanish means to shock, so every level says "hacer caer", with Readable first saying plainly what the fall is.
